title: Permission lineage export and phased dual-write throttle playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Ship a migration playbook that minimizes customer disruption for large orgs when moving from RBAC v1 -> RBAC v2 by (1) exporting per-organization permission lineage for visibility, (2) running a controlled, token-bucket backed backfill and dual-write throttling system, (3) validating audit-log parity and SSO/SAML mapping, and (4) providing admin rollback and communications artifacts.

Motivation: Several prior migration attempts tripped on unbounded backfills and slow parity detection in audit streams. Large orgs (>=10k users, 1000 teams) need pacing controls and a human-readable permission-lineage dump so security teams can validate changes before cutover. This ticket ties telemetry, backfill pacing, and customer-facing artifacts into a single operable playbook for on-call and PMs.

Non-goals: Rewriting the core authorization engine, or implementing a universal reconciliation operator for all legacy edge-cases. This is an operational runbook + engineering gating surface to complete the migration safely.
acceptance_criteria: Permission lineage export tool (org-scoped) produces NDJSON with subject->resource->permission chains and a signature hash; exported files available in customer S3 or secured Drive link.
Backfill job uses per-org token-bucket (configurable rate, burst) with observability (tokens remaining, backlog size) and can be paused/resumed via Console and CLI.

Dual-write path deployed in shadow mode for 7 days for internal customers and 3 external pilot customers; divergence rates calculated and dashboarded (acceptable threshold <0.3% for pilot before enabling for rest).
Audit-log parity check implemented: event-compare job that compares v1 and v2 authorization events for last 30 days; mismatch alerts routed to security and oncall.
SSO/SAML assertion harmonization tool runs per-customer; mapping warnings surfaced and stored as part of the lineage export.
Playbook includes explicit rollback steps, admin-safe short-circuits, and customer comms templates (opt-in window, risk notice, rollback notice).
Production canary run (two small orgs) completed with defined KPIs: no more than 1% elevation in 5xxs, no more than 5% increase in mean authorization latency, and audit divergence <0.3%.
implementation_steps: 1) Build permission-lineage-export service (CLI + job) that walks RBAC graph and emits NDJSON; include checksum meta and obfuscation flags for PII.
2) Implement per-org token-bucket controller inside backfill worker; expose rate, burst, and 'fast-path' whitelist for emergency ops.
3) Build dual-write shadow pipeline: write to v2 store while reading from v1 at runtime; persist divergence deltas with contextual sample events.
4) Create audit-compare job to replay last N days of events and compute parity metrics; surface in Console and Alerting.
5) Add SSO/SAML mapping validator to the export tool; include suggested mapping fixes when ambiguous nameIDs or attributes are found.
6) Wire console toggles: per-org backfill rate, dual-write shadow enable, and 'pause cutover' emergency button linked to oncall workflow.
7) Draft and review customer comms (opt-in timeline, expected behavior, rollback policy) with legal and support; prepare templates in Drive.
8) Run internal canaries -> pilot external customers (3) -> phased org waves with telemetry gates and automated rollback triggers.
9) Post-cutover: run weekly parity checks for 30 days and schedule follow-up audit export for customers.
10) Retrospective and playbook update captured in Confluence; add runbook checklist for SRE and Security teams.
risks: Large backfills might saturate DB read capacity if not properly paced — mitigated by token-bucket and read-replica routing.
Divergence detection lag could produce false confidence; we need high-fidelity sampling and deterministic event hashing to reduce noise.
Permission-lineage exports may contain sensitive identifiers — must support redaction and per-customer storage controls.
SSO/SAML assertion mismatches may block certain customers; provide fallbacks (manual mapping UI) and prioritize high-revenue accounts.
Operator error during cutover could enable admin-impersonation paths unintentionally; include explicit safety interlocks and two-person approval for final cutover.
Edge-case policies (templated policy languages) might not map 1:1; these will be flagged for manual review and migration assistants.

2026-02-18 Ops Note: Added automatic pause trigger when audit-mismatch-rate > 0.5% sustained over 5 minutes. Implemented token-bucket telemetry to Grafana dashboard.
